proposals.before: Book of Sui, 79th year of Volume, 44th year of Biographies
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English invents 'year of' for 卷/列傳 volume and biography numbers.

proposals.before: When Emperor Wu of Zhou entered the passes, Xin left his parents, wife, and children behind and went west to Chang'an, rising to high office; Luo was left behind and taken prisoner by the Northern Qi.
proposals.after: When Emperor Wu entered the passes, Xin left his parents, wife, and children behind and went west to Chang'an, rising to high office; Luo was left behind and taken prisoner by the Gao clan.
proposals.reason: Chinese has 武帝 after Xin served Wei (魏), not 周武帝; English invents 'of Zhou'. 高氏 is the Gao clan, not necessarily glossed as Northern Qi in the Chinese clause.

proposals.before: When Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou entered the passes, Xin abandoned his parents, wife, and children and returned west to Chang'an, passing through offices of eminent rank; because of this Luo was thereupon taken prisoner by the Gao clan.
proposals.after: When Emperor Wu entered the passes, Xin abandoned his parents, wife, and children and returned west to Chang'an, passing through offices of eminent rank; because of this Luo was thereupon taken prisoner by the Gao clan.
proposals.reason: Literal adds 'of Northern Zhou' absent from 武帝 in this Wei-service context.

proposals.before: That year Cong sent Grand General Qi Xin with a naval force to strike Chen's An commandery but failed and returned.
proposals.after: That year Cong sent Grand General Qi Xin with a naval force to strike Chen's Gong'an but failed and returned.
proposals.reason: 公安 is the place Gong'an, not 'An commandery'.

proposals.before: That year Cong sent the Grand General Qi Xin with a naval force to strike Chen's An commandery but failed and returned.
proposals.after: That year Cong sent the Grand General Qi Xin with a naval force to strike Chen Gong'an but failed and returned.
proposals.reason: 公安 should be Gong'an, not An commandery.

proposals.before: Su said, "The Qian'er are Diang; the Houmochen are barbarians—how can they be compared!"
proposals.after: Su said, "The Qian'er are Qiang; the Houmochen are barbarians—how can they be compared!"

proposals.after: Su meant that barbarians ranked above the Qiang.

proposals.after: Su's meaning was that barbarians were superior and Qiang inferior.

proposals.after: Cong said, "That the Qiang differ from barbarians is something I have never heard before."

proposals.before: The emperor referred the case to the high officials. Duke Niuzhang Niu Hong said, "Such evil rises through men. Kill the man and it will end."
proposals.after: The emperor referred the case to the high officials. Niu Hong, Duke of Qizhang, said, "Such evil rises through men. Kill the man and it will end."
proposals.reason: 奇章公 is Duke of Qizhang; 'Niuzhang' reverses and fuses the title with the surname.

decisions.reason: s0001 is 隋書卷七十九列傳第四十四: 卷 and 列傳 mark volume and biography numbers, not years. '79th/44th year of' invents wording absent from the Chinese; Volume 79, Biographies 44 matches the title formula.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 隋書卷七十九列傳第四十四

decisions.reason: After 初仕魏, the text has only 武帝之入關也, not 周武帝; 信後仕周 follows later, so 'of Zhou' is an invented polity. The prisoner clause is 為高氏所囚, which is the Gao clan, not the gloss 'Northern Qi'.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 武帝之入關也……羅由是遂為高氏所囚

decisions.reason: The Chinese reads 武帝之入關也 in a Wei-service sequence (s0034 仕魏; Zhou service only at s0036). Adding 'of Northern Zhou' is unsupported by 武帝 here; stripping that gloss restores the text.
襲陳公安 names the place 公安 (Gong'an), not a commandery 安. 'An commandery' mis-parses the toponym; Chen's Gong'an is accurate.
Literal likewise misread 公安 as 'An commandery'. The target is Gong'an under Chen; Chen Gong'an matches 陳公安.
素曰：「鉗耳，羌也」: 羌 is the ethnonym Qiang. 'Diang' is a mistranscription with no basis in the character.
The literal quotes the same 羌; Qiang is the correct reading, Diang is erroneous.
素意以虜優羌劣 uses 羌, so the ranked group is the Qiang, not 'Diang'.
Literal mirrors 羌劣; Qiang is required and Diang is wrong.
琮曰：「以羌異虜」 again has 羌; Cong's reply concerns the Qiang, not Diang.
The literal must render 羌 as Qiang; Diang invents a different name.
奇章公牛弘 is title 奇章公 plus name 牛弘. 'Duke Niuzhang' fuses and rearranges the fief title with the surname; Niu Hong, Duke of Qizhang is the correct parse.
